identity.title: AdAEM: An Adaptively and Automated Extensible Measurement of LLMs' Value Difference

problem.claim: Measure differences in LLM values to compare misalignment, cultural adaptability, and biases.

gap.claim: Existing methods often use outdated, contaminated, or generic questions that mainly capture shared safety orientations, producing indistinguishable results.

contributions.claim: Introduces AdAEM, a self-extensible evaluation algorithm that automatically and adaptively generates test questions by probing value boundaries across diverse LLMs.
Frames question generation as maximizing an information-theoretic objective intended to surface controversial topics that distinguish models’ value differences.
Releases the implementation and generated evaluation questions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish AdAEM from static benchmarks through automatic, adaptive, and extensible question generation that can co-evolve with LLM development.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AdAEM generated novel questions and supported an extensive analysis demonstrating the method’s validity and effectiveness.
The authors state that the question-generation process theoretically maximizes an information-theoretic objective for extracting diverse, controversial topics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Value differences are relevant for comparing LLM misalignment, cultural adaptability, and biases.
Static or generic question sets may fail to distinguish models because they measure orientations shared across LLMs.
AdAEM adaptively generates and extends questions by probing value boundaries across culturally and temporally diverse models.
Its information-theoretic framing targets diverse controversial topics and aims to track changing model values over time.
The authors report an extensive analysis using generated questions and release code and questions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a measurement failure—indistinguishable results—to an adaptive question-generation mechanism designed around information gain.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes the proposed method directly responsive to the stated informativeness gap.
lessons.application: When presenting an evaluation method, map the failure mode to an explicit design objective and mechanism, then state how the mechanism addresses it.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the task requires fixed, stable questions for longitudinal comparability or regulatory auditing.

unknowns: The abstract does not report datasets, model counts, evaluation metrics, baselines, quantitative results, or details of the claimed validity and effectiveness.
The assumptions and formal conditions behind the information-theoretic maximization are unspecified.
It is unclear how consistently the approach tracks value dynamics or how generated questions are quality-controlled.
